newsitem.title: USA: Brazil announces yields, rates for Brady exchange.
newsitem.headline: Brazil announces yields, rates for Brady exchange.

text.p: Brazil on Monday set a minimum yield of 9.946 percent for its $1.0 billion global bond issue, according to lead managers Goldman Sachs & Co and J.P. Morgan Securities.
The yield is the U.S. Treasury benchmark rate for the Global bonds of 6.946 percent plus the minimum clearing spread of 3.0 percent.

In addition, dealers said the Brady Bond exchange yield for Brazil's par bonds is 9.446 percent, or the Treasury benchmark rate for par bonds of 6.946 percent plus 2.5 percent. The Brady Bond exchange yield for Brazil's C bonds is 11.255 percent, or the Treasury benchmark rate for C bonds of 6.655 percent plus 4.6 percent.
The exchange price for par bonds is $653.40 per $1000 principal amount and the exchange price for C bonds is $877.82 per $1000 principal amount.
The discount bond exchange price is $818.75 per $1000 principal amount, managers added.

The benchmark rate for the global and par bonds of 6.946 percent is equal to the yield to maturity corresponding to Monday's 1500 EDT/1900 GMT bid price for the Treasury 6.50 percent bond due November 2026. The benchmark rate for C bonds of 6.655 percent is equal to the yield corresponding to Monday's 1500 EDT/1900 GMT bid price for the Treasury 6.625 percent bond due May 2007.

Brazil's debt swap allows investors to tender their par bonds, discount bond or C bond for the 30-year global bond issue or to purchase outright the new issue. The invitation is scheduled to expire at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT on Tuesday.
